PASS. The diff cleanly implements PMAT-065 (#65) and matches all acceptance criteria and receipt claims without touching out-of-scope files or weakening any gate.

Scope question answer: Yes, gating on `book-build` alone is right. `book-build` (using mdBook v0.4.40, matching `pages.yml`) is the only check that is proven green on `main`. Wiring checks that have never passed on `main` (link check #58, `mdbook test`, `test.yml` chapter matrix #53/#56, `pmat-dogfood.yml`) into the required `gate` fan-in would leave every PR permanently unmergeable, defeating the ticket's goal. Requiring three green nights on `main` plus explicit owner sign-off before graduating additional jobs into `gate.needs` is the right discipline.

findings.claim: .github/workflows/gate.yml defines the required `gate` fan-in job triggered on pull_request, push, merge_group, and workflow_dispatch, with `if: always()` and `needs: [book-build]`, failing when `needs` is empty (`total -eq 0`) or any needed job result is not `success` (`bad -ne 0`).

The implementation receipt accurately documents the workflow triggers, jobs, planted GitHub Actions control runs (green, red, vacuous), and quorum rounds.
